Lumenix: provide staging access and synthetic traffic bucket by 2026-10-11
action_items: Alicia Park - Share final cutover runbook and canary threshold doc - due 2026-10-09
Marcus Chen - Produce run of smoke-test scripts and upload to shared folder - due 2026-10-12
Jamal Ortiz - Confirm synthetic traffic generator and baseline p95 numbers in staging - due 2026-10-11

summary: Weekly POC sync focused on final preflight tasks for staging cutover, canary and A/B rollback criteria, monitoring handoff, and assignment of owners for the dry-run. Agreed thresholds and visibility requirements; Redwood to deliver final runbook and telemetry checklist.
topics: Canary thresholds and metrics (p95, error rate, semantic correctness)
Dry-run schedule and synthetic traffic plan
transcript:
[00:00] Alicia Park: ok thanks everyone for joining, uh we're gonna run through the preflight checklist for the staging shift and the A over B rollback plan. we have about 55 minutes so we'll try to be tight. Marcus, you wanna kick off with canary metrics?
[00:18] Marcus Chen: sure, yeah. hi everyone. quick context — this week's run on staging showed steady throughput, kv cache hit rate improved with the new batching and we saw p95 at 210ms for the generation pipeline on the smaller seq lengths. there was an outlier on long seqs but that's expected.
[00:40] Sofia Rivera: and the long seqs were with the larger instruction sets? we saw a couple of timeouts yesterday in the logs.
[00:47] Marcus Chen: yeah, those were with 2.2k token requests hitting a cold kv cache. the fix is warmup + prefix caching, we demoed the warmup script; that will be part of the runbook.
[00:59] Tom Briggs: from security side, quick note — audit logs, we need proof of KMS integration and that logs are forwarded for 90 days. SOC 2 checklist item. is that in scope for the pilot?
[01:10] Alicia Park: yes, we flagged that last week. Redwood will hand over HSM/KMS integration notes and a sample audit log export. Marcus will attach the schema.
[01:19] Marcus Chen: I'll put the example export in the shared drive. also note we have a toggle to redact user PII in logs if you want, Tom.
[01:27] Tom Briggs: good. we do need retention set to 90 days and SSO for console access, SAML.
[01:33] Priya Nair: noted, we'll include SSO instructions in the runbook and the contact for enterprise support.
[01:38] Eliot Shaw: on the canary thresholds, what are we gating on exactly? we care about latency but also semantic accuracy — we had a test set where the rerank moved expected results.
[01:48] Marcus Chen: agreed. proposed gating: p95 latency change less than +10% vs staging baseline, error rate below 1% absolute, and semantic drift metric — rouge-like score drop not more than 3 points on the Lumenix prompt suite. also throughput capacity at 80% of expected peak.
[02:10] Sofia Rivera: that last bit — throughput — can we automate scaling? we don't want manual intervention during the canary.
[02:18] Marcus Chen: yes, autoscale policy in Dedicated mode available, but for this pilot in staging we'll run a scripted burst step in the runbook to validate autoscale triggers.
[02:27] Jamal Ortiz: who runs that scripted burst? our SRE or Redwood?
[02:30] Alicia Park: Redwood will run the first dry-run with synthetic traffic, then we'll hand the run to Lumenix SRE for the second rehearsal. responsibilities are in the action items.
[02:40] Eliot Shaw: and if the canary fails the semantic check but latency is fine, what's the rollback? do we automatically switch traffic back to previous model?
[02:48] Marcus Chen: recommended flow: automated rollback if any hard alert fires (ex: error rate > 1% or p95 spike > 25%). for semantic regressions, initially we run an A/B with traffic weighting — if semantic score delta exceeds threshold for two consecutive evaluation windows (15m windows) then auto-terminate new model traffic and escalate. the runbook defines manual override as well.
[03:12] Sofia Rivera: okay, A/B where we run 20% new / 80% old for 30 minutes then expand to 50/50 if green?
[03:19] Marcus Chen: exactly. our suggested canary ramp: 5% for 10 minutes, 20% for 20 minutes, 50% for 30 minutes, with metric evaluation at each step.
[03:30] Tom Briggs: what's the exact metric window for p95? you said 10/20/30 minutes, but p95 needs enough samples.
[03:36] Marcus Chen: we use sliding 15-minute windows; thresholds must hold for two consecutive windows at critical gates.
[03:41] Alicia Park: let's capture that: sliding 15m windows, two-window confirmation at the 20% and 50% gates.
[03:48] Sofia Rivera: monitoring — we use Datadog dashboards. can Redwood push telemetry to our Datadog account?
[03:55] Marcus Chen: yes, we support forwarding metrics to Datadog and Prometheus scrape endpoints. we'll provide a telemetry checklist with metric names, tags, and sample queries.
[04:03] Priya Nair: also we'll include NR/alert runbooks for paging and escalation. who is on call for the first 24 hours?
[04:10] Jamal Ortiz: Lumenix will own application-level alerts; Redwood will be on-call for model-serving infra for the pilot window. contacts listed in runbook.
[04:18] Marcus Chen: adding to that, we will provide playbooks for graceful degradation — e.g., reduce max tokens and fall back to smaller model variant if latency breaches SLO.
[04:26] Eliot Shaw: fallback to smaller variant — how do we quantify acceptable quality drop? product needs a clear SLA.
[04:32] Marcus Chen: we recommend a quality budget: no more than 5% decrease in our internal score across the core user flows during fallback. that will be included in the telemetry doc.
[04:43] Alicia Park: okay next — cutover sequence. Marcus?
[04:46] Marcus Chen: cutover sequence in runbook: 1) freeze deploys, 2) snapshot config, 3) run smoke tests, 4) push 5% traffic, evaluate, 5) follow ramp plan. smoke tests include a small synthetic suite (approx 200 requests) and basic end-to-end checks.
[05:03] Sofia Rivera: what's the expected time for snapshot and rollback? can we rollback in under 3 minutes?
[05:08] Marcus Chen: automated rollback is generally sub-2 minutes for connection re-route; model warmup can add time if variant requires loading, so we keep small initial percentages to avoid warmup latency.
[05:18] Tom Briggs: audit trail — we need clear logging of who initiated rollbacks or overrides.
[05:23] Alicia Park: Redwood console logs admin actions and we'll include a sample export.
[05:27] Marcus Chen: small caveat, the transcript labeling from the meeting tool sometimes mis-attrib — excuse me — but we'll make sure the runbook owners are explicit.
[05:36] Eliot Shaw: dry-run schedule — we earlier proposed 10/13 for rehearsals, can we do two dry-runs, one internal and one with production traffic shadowed?
[05:45] Alicia Park: yes. plan: 10/13 internal Redwood-led dry-run in staging, 10/15 joint rehearsals with partial production shadowing (no real traffic cutover), and final window on 10/20 for go/no-go decision.
[05:58] Jamal Ortiz: we need the final traffic steering spreadsheet to run our chaos tests.
[06:02] Marcus Chen: sending that today after call, it includes canary percentages, metric checks, and rollback steps.
[06:09] Sofia Rivera: any dependencies from infra— VPC peering, route tables? we had some issues last time.
[06:14] Alicia Park: Redwood team to validate VPC routes in staging; we'll include a connection validation checklist.
[06:20] Tom Briggs: security sign-off steps: KMS proof, SAML working, audit log retention, and penetration test scheduling if required.
[06:28] Priya Nair: we'll attach the security docs and link to SOC 2 artifacts. expected sign-off by 10/10.
[06:34] Marcus Chen: ok i'll summarize canary gates: p95 delta < +10% (sliding 15m windows, 2 windows), error rate < 1% absolute, semantic score delta < -3 points, throughput capacity >= 80% baseline. auto-rollback on hard thresholds, A/B rollback for semantic regressions.
[06:51] Eliot Shaw: sounds good. on escalation, who does Lumenix call first? Redwood primary on-call: Marcus, backup: Alicia?
[06:58] Marcus Chen: correct. contact numbers in runbook.
[07:03] Alicia Park: any open questions?
[07:06] Sofia Rivera: only one — can you include a short checklist for our legal/procurement team regarding reserved capacity terms?
[07:11] Alicia Park: yes, Priya will add a short reserved capacity summary and the options.
[07:15] Priya Nair: will do, and also include the pricing link and escalation contacts.
[07:20] Marcus Chen: last note: we'll add a short step in the runbook to verify KV cache warmup for long-seq flows before increasing traffic.
[07:27] Alicia Park: great. recap of next steps and owners in the action items. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the runbook and schedule invites for dry-runs.
[07:36] (meeting ends)
notes: Meeting contained natural transcription noise and a few misattributed speaker labels typical of Fireflies exports
